mainTopic: בן סורר ומורה: meat and wine, stealing from his father, the parents' requirements, and laws that 'never happened'
overview: A בן סורר ומורה is only liable if he eats meat and drinks wine, learned from 'זולל וסובא', with a hint from משלי. רבי זירא uses that same פסוק to warn against sleeping in the בית המדרש. A משנה teaches that he must steal from his father and eat on someone else's property, because only then is stealing easy and he has no fear. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires stealing from his mother too, and the גמרא explains how a mother can own anything. The next משנה requires both parents to want the case. רבי יהודה adds that the mother must match the father, which the גמרא explains as the same voice, appearance and height. This leads to ברייתות saying a בן סורר ומורה, an עיר הנדחת and a בית המנוגע never happened, each matched to a strict תנא and each answered by eyewitness reports. A final משנה excludes parents with physical disabilities and describes the flogging-then-trial process, and the גמרא begins to ask whether every פסוק must be fulfilled exactly as written. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the previous discussion: he is liable
steps.stepSummary: The single word חייב ends the earlier discussion about someone drinking wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes the discussion from the previous page. It is not the start of anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier sugya was dealing with someone who drank wine. It ends with the ruling that he is חייב. The new topic starts in the next line.

phrases.english: He is liable.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the earlier case: he's liable for entering the מקדש after drinking wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a discussion that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the earlier case, the person is liable.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: he must eat meat and drink wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה it is about to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not become a בן סורר ומורה unless he eats meat and drinks wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה. It is setting up the next move, where a ברייתא will explain the rule and give its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a narrow requirement: only meat and wine count. The גמרא now wants to find the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The stubborn and rebellious son of דברים 21

phrases.english: He does not become a stubborn and rebellious son
unless he eats meat and drinks wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר וְיִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the earlier discussion closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only eating meat and drinking wine can make a boy a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: ברייתא: other food and drink don't count, based on 'זולל וסובא'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that other foods and drinks do not count, and learns this from the words 'a glutton and a drunkard'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if he ate any food but not meat, or drank any drink but not wine, he is not a בן סורר ומורה. He must eat meat and drink wine, as the פסוק says 'a glutton and a drunkard'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the משנה and shows where the rule comes from in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out that eating plenty of other foods, or drinking other drinks, is not enough. The words 'זולל' (glutton) and 'סובא' (drunkard) are read as pointing to meat and wine.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כׇּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: If he ate any food but did not eat meat,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁתָה כׇּל מַשְׁקֶה וְלֹא שָׁתָה יַיִן –
phrases.english: or drank any drink but did not drink wine,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son
unless he eats meat and drinks wine,
as it is said: "A glutton and a drunkard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that only meat and wine count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, reading 'זולל וסובא' in דברים 21:20.

steps.title: A hint from משלי linking meat and wine
steps.stepSummary: There is no clear proof that זולל means meat and סובא means wine, but פסוקים in משלי hint at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no real proof, there is a hint: 'Be not among wine drinkers, among gluttonous eaters of meat', and also 'For the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor, and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It admits it has no hard proof that these words mean meat and wine, so it brings a hint from משלי instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משלי, 'סובא' appears next to wine and 'זולל' next to meat. That is a hint, not a strict proof. The second פסוק shows that these same words describe someone whose eating and drinking ruins him.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no proof for the matter
A hint or allusion to the matter
And it also says (brings another פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: A 'זכר לדבר' is only a hint. The ברייתא openly says it is not a full proof.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָיה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And although there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter, as it is said:
"Be not among wine drinkers,
among gluttonous eaters of meat."
And it says: "For the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor,
and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָיה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds outside support for reading זולל and סובא as meat and wine.
steps.raayaObject: That זולל means eating meat and סובא means drinking wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 23:20-21, given only as a hint.

steps.title: רבי זירא: sleeping in the בית המדרש leaves one's Torah in rags
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reads the same פסוק as a warning about sleeping in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: anyone who sleeps in the בית המדרש, his Torah will become torn into rags, as it says 'and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side lesson. רבי זירא uses the last פסוק quoted to teach something about Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says drowsiness leads to rags. רבי זירא applies this to learning: someone who dozes off in the בית המדרש ends up with Torah knowledge full of holes, in pieces instead of whole.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Anyone who sleeps in the study hall,
his Torah becomes torn into rags,
as it is said: "And drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק just quoted and draws a separate lesson from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping in the בית המדרש leaves a person's Torah in pieces.
steps.whatToRemember: A בן סורר ומורה needs meat and wine, learned from 'זולל וסובא', with a hint from משלי. רבי זירא uses that same פסוק to warn against sleeping in the בית המדרש.

steps.title: משנה: he must steal from his father and eat on others' property
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists three cases that do not count. Only stealing from his father and eating on someone else's property counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole from his father and ate on his father's property, or stole from others and ate on others' property, or stole from others and ate on his father's property, he is not a בן סורר ומורה. He must steal from his father and eat on others' property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It adds another requirement: where the food comes from and where he eats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two things to check: whose food it was, and whose property he ate on. Of the combinations, only one makes him a בן סורר ומורה: food stolen from his father, eaten on someone else's property. The משנה does not give a reason here.
steps.confusionAlert: Stealing from other people does not count, even if he eats on his father's property. The food must come from his father.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: גָּנַב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וְאָכַל בִּרְשׁוּת אָבִיו,
phrases.english: If he stole from his father's things and ate on his father's property,
or from others' things and ate on others' property,
or from others' things and ate on his father's property,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son
unless he steals from his father's things
and eats on others' property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ גָּנַב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וְאָכַל בִּרְשׁוּת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה with another condition for בן סורר ומורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He becomes a בן סורר ומורה only if he steals from his father and eats on others' property.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: from both father and mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires that the stolen food come from both his father and his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: not unless he steals from his father and from his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the משנה adds a stricter condition to the rule just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion only mentions stealing from the father. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says stealing from the father alone is not enough; he must also steal from his mother.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, son of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּגְנוֹב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וּמִשֶּׁל אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: Not unless he steals from his father's things and from his mother's things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion by adding a stricter requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He must steal from both his father and his mother.
steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion in the משנה: steal from his father and eat on others' property. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: he must steal from both his father and his mother.

steps.title: Stealing from father and eating at father's place: he is afraid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why stealing from his father and eating on his father's property does not count. It is easy for him to steal, but he is afraid of being caught.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: If he stole from his father and ate on his father's property, even though stealing is easy for him, he is afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the reasons behind the משנה's list of cases, beginning with the first one: stolen from father, eaten at father's place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא uses two tests: is it easy for him to steal, and is he afraid? Here stealing from his father is easy, but eating right in his father's home makes him scared of being seen. That fear keeps him from being pulled into worse behavior, so he is not a בן סורר ומורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is easy and available for him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one good factor is enough. The גמרא is setting up a rule that BOTH factors must point toward danger: easy to steal AND no fear.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
If he stole from what belongs to his father
and ate it on his father's property,
even though it is easy for him to get,
he is afraid.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּנַב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וְאָכַל בִּרְשׁוּת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the משנה cases listed in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stealing from father and eating at father's place does not count, because he is afraid of being caught.

steps.title: Stealing from others: not easy for him
steps.stepSummary: Stealing from others and eating at their place does not count, because even without fear, stealing from strangers is not easy. Stealing from others and eating at his father's place is even more obviously excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole from others and ate on others' property, even though he is not afraid, it is not easy for him. And all the more so if he stole from others and ate on his father's property, where it is not easy for him and he is afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next two cases of the משנה using the same two tests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among strangers he has no fear, but stealing from strangers is hard, so he will not keep doing it. In the last case both tests fail: stealing from others is hard and eating at home is scary. So it obviously does not count (כל שכן).

phrases.english: If he stole from others and ate on others' property,
even though he is not afraid,
it is not easy for him to get.
And all the more so if he stole from others
and ate on his father's property,
where it is not easy for him and he is afraid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same two tests from step 8 to the משנה's other excluded cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stealing from others does not count, whether eaten at others' place or at his father's, because such stealing is not easy for him.

steps.title: The only case that counts: easy to steal and no fear
steps.stepSummary: He is only liable if he steals from his father and eats on others' property, since stealing is easy and he has no fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not liable unless he steals from his father and eats on others' property, because it is easy for him and he is not afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its explanation by giving the reason for the one case that does count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the only case where both tests point to danger. Stealing from his father is easy, and eating away from home means no fear of being caught. That combination is what can drag him into a life of crime.
steps.whatToRemember: Two tests: easy to steal (שכיח ליה) and no fear (לא בעית). Only stealing from father and eating elsewhere passes both, so only that makes him a בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: He is not liable unless he steals from his father
and eats on the property of others,
since it is easy for him, and he is not afraid.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁיִּגְנוֹב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו, וְיֹאכַל בִּרְשׁוּת אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation started in steps 8 and 9 by explaining the one case that counts.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liability requires stealing from the father and eating on others' property: easy access plus no fear.

steps.title: How can the mother own anything to steal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who requires stealing from the mother too, and asks how she can own anything if whatever a wife acquires belongs to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: unless he steals from his father and from his mother. His mother, where does she have anything? Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view from the משנה and challenges it with a basic rule about a wife's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that what a wife acquires belongs to her husband. If so, everything in the house is the father's, and there is nothing that is truly the mother's for the son to steal. So how can רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה require stealing from her?

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever a wife acquires, her husband acquires

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּגְנוֹב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וּמִשֶּׁל אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: Not unless he steals from his father and from his mother.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה we saw in step 7.

phrases.english: His mother, where would she have anything of her own?
Whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the reasoning about the first part of the משנה and returns to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's requirement to steal from the mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife's acquisitions belong to her husband, so the mother seems to own nothing that could be stolen from her.

steps.title: He stole from a meal set for both parents
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that the son stole from a meal prepared for his father and mother together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: from a meal prepared for his father and his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question by describing a case where the mother does have a share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a meal is set out for both parents, the food meant for the mother's meal is given to her by her husband. So stealing from that meal counts as stealing from both the father and the mother.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's 'father and mother' means food taken from a meal set out for both parents.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
He stole from a meal that was prepared for his father and his mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִסְּעוּדָה הַמּוּכֶנֶת לְאָבִיו וּלְאִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: defines a specific situation where the mother has a share
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother owns nothing, so the requirement to steal from her makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food from a meal set out for both parents belongs partly to the mother, so stealing from it is stealing from both.

steps.title: He must buy the food, not steal the food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of a meal prepared for both parents, citing רב הונא's rule that the son must purchase cheap meat and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב הונא said the son is only liable if he buys cheap meat and eats it, and buys cheap wine and drinks it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 12. If the son stole food from a ready meal, he didn't buy anything, yet רב הונא says he must buy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule means the son steals money and uses it to buy meat and wine. A son who grabs food straight off his parents' table does not fit that rule, so the answer from Step 12 seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (a challenge from another statement)

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabbi Chanan bar Molada say
that Rav Huna says:
He is not liable unless he buys
cheap meat and eats it,
phrases.notes: Buying means he stole money first, not the food itself. That's the problem with the meal answer.

phrases.english: and cheap wine and drinks it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן בַּר מוֹלָדָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer that the son stole from a meal prepared for both parents.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא requires the son to buy the meat and wine, which implies stolen money, not stolen food.

steps.title: He stole the money set aside for the parents' meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adjusts the answer: the son stole money meant for a meal for his father and mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say he stole from the money of a meal that was being prepared for his father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer so it fits רב הונא. The son took money that was set aside for both parents' meal, and then bought his meat and wine with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both pieces fit: the money belongs in some sense to the mother as well (it was meant for her meal), and the son still buys the food himself. Only the object stolen changed, from food to money.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (a corrected version of the answer)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
from the money of a meal
that was set aside for his father and for his mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by adjusting the answer of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the case (money instead of food)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son stole the food itself from the parents' meal, which clashes with רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son stole money set aside for both parents' meal and bought the food with it.

steps.title: A gift the husband cannot touch
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: someone gave the mother property on condition that her husband has no rights to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that someone else gave her property and told her: 'on condition that your husband has no rights in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to answer the question from Step 11. The mother really can own something, if a giver made it hers with a condition that keeps the husband out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original problem was that whatever a wife acquires belongs to her husband. This answer shows a case where it does not: the giver's condition makes it truly hers, so the son can steal from his mother.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say:
that someone else gave her property,
phrases.notes: "Her" is the mother. This answers the question from Step 11: how can she own anything?

phrases.english: and said to her:
"on condition that your husband has no rights in them."

steps.whatToRemember: The son can steal from his mother in two ways: money set aside for both parents' meal, or a gift given to her that her husband has no rights to.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the question in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case where the wife truly owns property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wife cannot own anything apart from her husband, so stealing from the mother is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gift given on condition that the husband has no rights in it belongs to her alone.

steps.title: Both parents must want it
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that the son is not a בן סורר ומורה unless both father and mother want to bring him to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his father wants and his mother doesn't, or his father doesn't want and his mother does, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה unless both of them want.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says both parents have to agree before the son can be judged as a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One parent alone is not enough, whether it is the father or the mother. Both must want to bring the case.

keyTerms.meaning: wants (here: wants to bring the son to court)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If his father wanted
and his mother did not want,
or his father did not want and his mother wanted –
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son
unless both of them want.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה אָבִיו רוֹצֶה וְאִמּוֹ אֵינָהּ רוֹצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after finishing the discussion of stealing from the mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son becomes a בן סורר ומורה only if both parents want to bring him to court.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the mother must be fit for the father
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that if the mother was not fit for the father, the son cannot become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if his mother was not fit for his father, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהודה's extra condition about the parents' match. It does not yet explain what 'not fit' means, so the גמרא will ask next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beyond both parents agreeing, רבי יהודה requires that the mother be a proper match for the father. The meaning of 'fit' becomes the next question, and step 20 answers it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ רְאוּיָה לְאָבִיו,
phrases.english: If his mother was not fit for his father,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further condition within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, if the mother was not fit for the father, the son cannot become a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: What does 'not fit' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה means by the mother being 'not fit' for the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not fit' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רבי יהודה's words. This sets up the next move, where it will test a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'not fit' could mean many things. The גמרא wants a precise definition before going further.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is "not fit"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי יהודה's phrase in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a mother who is 'not fit' for the father.

steps.title: Forbidden marriage? He is still their son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'not fit' means a union punishable by כרת or court death, then rejects it: the parents are still his father and mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a union punished by כרת or by court death penalties, in the end his father is his father and his mother is his mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one meaning of 'not fit' and immediately pushes back on it. A forbidden union still produces a real father and a real mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חייבי כריתות and חייבי מיתות בית דין, the marriage doesn't take effect. But the פסוקים speak of 'his father' and 'his mother', and that is still true here, so this can't be what רבי יהודה means.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposing a meaning to test it)
those whose union is punished by כרת
those whose union is punished by a court death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is concluding that 'not fit' means a forbidden union. It suggests it only to reject it, because he still has a real father and mother.

phrases.english: If you say: those liable to karet
and those liable to court death penalties,
in the end, his father is his father,
and his mother is his mother!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת וְחַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין, סוֹף סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first possible answer to the question in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'not fit' means a union of חייבי כריתות or חייבי מיתות בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even in a forbidden union, the boy still has a real father and mother, so there is no reason to exclude him.

steps.title: Not fit means not identical to the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה means the mother must be identical to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה is saying the mother must be the same as the father.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first explanation, the גמרא gives the real meaning of רבי יהודה's 'not fit': the mother must be the same as the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 showed that 'not fit' cannot mean a forbidden marriage, because they are still his parents. So the גמרא reads it as a physical match between the parents. The details of that match come in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, he means one who is identical to his father.
phrases.notes: "One" here is the mother. רבי יהודה means she must be like the father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted reading after step 19 rejected the first reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not fit' means a marriage forbidden with כרת or court death.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not fit' means the mother is not identical to the father.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms: same voice, appearance and height
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying the mother must match the father in voice, appearance and height.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, if his mother was not the same as his father in voice, appearance and height, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing it just explained, and spells out what 'identical' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports step 20's reading of רבי יהודה. It also adds the three details: voice, appearance and height.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ שָׁוָה לְאָבִיו
phrases.english: If his mother was not identical to his father
in voice, in appearance, and in height,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that רבי יהודה requires the mother to be identical to the father.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה directly.

steps.title: Why must the parents be identical?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה gets this rule. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but not the reason. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק it comes from.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring the parents to be identical.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'our voice'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'our voice' in the singular, so the parents must share one voice, and so also appearance and height.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says, 'He does not listen to our voice.' Since we need them to be the same in voice, we also need them to be the same in appearance and height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the parents say 'our voice,' as if the two of them have one voice. From that it extends the rule to appearance and height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two parents speaking with one 'voice' shows they must sound the same. Once the Torah wants them the same in one way, the גמרא extends this to looks and height as well.

keyTerms.meaning: to our voice (one voice for both parents)

phrases.english: As the verse says:
"He does not listen to our voice."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:20. "Our voice" is one voice for two people, so they must sound alike.

phrases.english: Since in voice we require them to be identical,
in appearance and height we also require them to be identical.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'our voice' shows one shared voice, and this extends to appearance and height.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, a son can only be a בן סורר ומורה if his mother and father are the same in voice, appearance and height, based on 'our voice.'

steps.title: Who holds that a rebellious son never happened?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the ברייתא saying a בן סורר ומורה never was and never will be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא: A בן סורר ומורה never was and never will be. So why was it written? Learn it and get reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says this law never actually happens, and asks which תנא it fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah wrote a law that never happens, someone must hold conditions so strict that it can't really occur. The גמרא wants to find who that is.

keyTerms.meaning: never was and never will be

phrases.english: Whose opinion does this follow, which was taught:
A stubborn and rebellious son
never was and never will be.
So why was it written?
Learn it and receive reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that ties into how strict רבי יהודה's conditions are.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view makes a בן סורר ומורה impossible in practice.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean the law is not real. It is a real Torah law, but its conditions are so strict that it never actually happens.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, whose conditions make the case practically impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose? רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parents who are identical in voice, appearance and height almost never exist. So for רבי יהודה, a בן סורר ומורה would never actually happen.

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, because his requirement of identical parents is almost impossible to meet.

steps.title: Or it follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who can't accept stoning a boy just for eating meat and drinking wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say it is רבי שמעון. As taught: רבי שמעון said, just because this boy ate a תרטימר of meat and drank half a לוג of Italian wine, his father and mother take him out to stone him? Rather, it never was and never will be. So why was it written? Learn it and get reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another possible answer: the ברייתא could be רבי שמעון. He says it makes no sense to kill a boy just for this eating and drinking, so it never happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's reason is technical: the parents must match. רבי שמעון's reason is about logic: the punishment seems too harsh for the act, so the case must never really happen. Both lead to 'never was and never will be,' but for different reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: a set amount of meat, the amount in the משנה
half a לוג, a liquid measure

phrases.english: If you want, say: it is Rabbi Shimon.
As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
Is it just because this one ate
a tarteimar of meat
and drank half a log of Italian wine,
that his father and mother take him out to stone him?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לֹא הָיָה וְלֹא עָתִיד לִהְיוֹת,
phrases.english: Rather, it never was and never will be.
So why was it written? Learn it and receive reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 24, in place of רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון, who says the case never happens because the punishment does not seem to fit the act.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: I saw one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says a בן סורר ומורה did happen: he saw one and sat on his grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: I saw him and sat on his grave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן disagrees with the ברייתא. He says this case really did happen, because he saw it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said it never happened. רבי יונתן answers with what he saw with his own eyes: a real בן סורר ומורה who was put to death and buried.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:
I saw him
and I sat on his grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the claim in steps 24 and 26 that it never happened.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a בן סורר ומורה never was and never will be.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores a real case that רבי יונתן saw himself.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a disagreement: רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון holds a בן סורר ומורה never happens, but רבי יונתן says he saw one.

steps.title: Who holds that an idolatrous city never happened?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the ברייתא saying an עיר הנדחת never was and never will be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא: An עיר הנדחת never was and never will be. So why was it written? Learn it and get reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about another Torah law, the idolatrous city: who holds it never happens?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This copies the pattern of step 24, now for עיר הנדחת. The גמרא looks for the תנא whose rules make it impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: a city whose people turned to idol worship

phrases.english: Whose opinion does this follow, which was taught:
An idolatrous city
never was and never will be.
So why was it written? Learn it and receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא: עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a parallel question to step 24 about a different law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view makes an עיר הנדחת impossible in practice.

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר: even one מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who says a city with even one מזוזה cannot become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose? רבי אליעזר's. As taught: רבי אליעזר says, any city that has even one מזוזה cannot become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and quotes his rule about a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Almost every Jewish city has at least one מזוזה. So according to רבי אליעזר, a city will practically never qualify as an עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: the scroll fixed on a doorpost

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Eliezer.
As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Any city that has in it
even one mezuza
does not become an idolatrous city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, since nearly every city has a מזוזה.
steps.whatToRemember: Both בן סורר ומורה and עיר הנדחת have a ברייתא saying they never happen, matched to a תנא whose conditions make them practically impossible: רבי יהודה (or רבי שמעון) for the son, and רבי אליעזר for the city.

steps.title: Why Does a מזוזה Block an Idolatrous City?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's rule that one מזוזה prevents a city from becoming an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why one מזוזה stops a city from becoming an עיר הנדחת. This short question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step we learned רבי אליעזר's rule, but not his source. Here the גמרא asks what makes a single מזוזה so powerful.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people turned to עבודה זרה. The city is destroyed.
The holy scroll fixed on a doorpost

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He's asking why even one מזוזה stops a city from becoming an עיר הנדחת, as רבי אליעזר said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for saying one מזוזה prevents an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: All the Spoil Must Be Burned, but a מזוזה May Not Be Destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The Torah requires burning all the spoil of an עיר הנדחת. Destroying a holy item like a מזוזה is forbidden, so the burning can't be done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And all its spoil you shall gather into the middle of its square and burn with fire.' Since, if there is a מזוזה, this is impossible, as it is written: 'You shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two פסוקים. One says to burn everything in the city. The other forbids destroying holy things like a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of עיר הנדחת demands that ALL the spoil be burned. A מזוזה contains ה׳'s name, and erasing it is forbidden. So in a city with a מזוזה, 'burn everything' cannot be fully carried out, and the city cannot become an עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: Its spoil, meaning everything in the city
And you shall burn with fire
You shall not do so. This is the source for not destroying holy things.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'And all its spoil you shall gather'
into the middle of its square and burn with fire.'
And since, if there is a מזוזה,
it is impossible,
as it is written: 'You shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:4. It comes right after the command to destroy idols, so it teaches: don't destroy what is holy to ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצוה of burning all the spoil conflicts with the ban on destroying a holy object. So a city with a מזוזה cannot become an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: I Sat on Its Ruins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן rejects the claim that an עיר הנדחת never existed. He says he saw one and sat on its ruins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: I saw it and sat on its mound of ruins.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as he did for בן סורר ומורה, רבי יונתן says that an עיר הנדחת really did happen. He saw its ruins himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said an עיר הנדחת never was and never will be. רבי יונתן answers with an eyewitness report. This shows the ruling against it is not the only view.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage who gives eyewitness reports against the 'never happened' claims

steps.whatToRemember: An עיר הנדחת is 'impossible' only according to רבי אליעזר's מזוזה rule. רבי יונתן says one actually existed.

phrases.english: רבי יונתן said:
I saw it and sat on its mound of ruins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the ברייתא explained in steps 28 and 29, just as step 27 did for בן סורר ומורה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא's claim that an עיר הנדחת never happened
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts the eyewitness evidence: רבי יונתן saw such a city.

steps.title: Who Says a Leprous House Never Happened?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the ברייתא that says a בית המנוגע never was and never will be, and was written only to be studied.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom is that which is taught in a ברייתא: A house afflicted with צרעת never was and never will be. And why was it written? Study it and receive reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a third 'never happened' ברייתא, this time about a house with צרעת. It asks whose opinion that ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the same question pattern used for בן סורר ומורה and עיר הנדחת. The ברייתא says the purpose of the Torah's section on house-צרעת is only the reward for learning it.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which is taught in a ברייתא:
A house afflicted with צרעת never was
and never will be,
And why was it written?
Study it and receive reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'which תנא?' pattern from step 28 to a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a בית המנוגע can never actually happen.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון's Corner Requirement
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He requires the mark to appear in a very specific way: on two stones, in two walls, right at a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom? Like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, as we learned in a משנה: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, a house never becomes impure until a mark is seen the size of two split beans, on two stones, in two walls, at a corner. Its length is like two split beans and its width like one split bean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. His conditions for house-צרעת are so precise that they would almost never all happen together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mark must be the size of two גריסין, spread across two stones, sitting in two walls that meet at a corner, with exact measurements. All of this together is so unlikely that the case is practically impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי
A split bean, used as a size measure for נגעים
A corner, where two walls meet

phrases.english: Like whom? Like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: as we learned in a משנה: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says,
a house never becomes impure
until a mark is seen the size of two split beans
on two stones
in two walls at a corner,
its length like two split beans
and its width like one split bean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, whose strict conditions make house-צרעת almost impossible.

steps.title: Where Does the Corner Requirement Come From?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's rule that the mark must be in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires the corner. This sets up the פסוק-based answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two walls at a corner' condition is what makes the case so rare. So the גמרא wants to see where this condition comes from.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring the mark to be at a corner.

steps.title: 'Wall' and 'Walls': A Corner
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses both 'wall' (singular) and 'walls' (plural). One wall that counts as two walls is a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'wall,' and it is written 'walls.' Which wall is like walls? You must say: this is a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the Torah uses both the singular 'קיר' and the plural 'קירות.' The only place that fits both words is a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A corner is one spot that is also part of two walls, so it is 'a wall that is like walls.' This settles both words in the פסוק and gives the source for the corner rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say. It introduces the only possible answer.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that says 'בית המנוגע never happened' follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He learns from קיר/קירות that the mark must be in a corner, which almost never happens.

phrases.english: It is written 'wall,' and it is written 'walls.'
Which wall is like walls?
You must say: this is a corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular and plural words in the פסוק together point to a corner.

steps.title: The 'Closed-Up Ruin' near Gaza
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק reports a place near Gaza called 'the closed-up ruin,' which shows a leprous house really existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק said, there was a place in the area of Gaza, and they used to call it 'the closed-up ruin.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings eyewitness evidence against the claim that a בית המנוגע never happened. A ruin near Gaza was known by a name that points to house-צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors רבי יונתן's replies about בן סורר ומורה and עיר הנדחת. The name of the place shows that a house there had been condemned for צרעת and torn down.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who reports what he knew from his time
The 'closed-up ruin,' the ruin of a house shut up for צרעת

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק,
phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק said,
there was a place in the area of Gaza,
and they used to call it
'the closed-up ruin.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the ברייתא of step 33 with a report that a בית המנוגע really existed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a בית המנוגע never happened
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A known ruin near Gaza shows that one did happen.

steps.title: Leprous Stones Dumped in the Galilee
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון איש כפר עכו adds that he saw a marked-off place in the Galilee where leprous stones had been dumped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון איש כפר עכו said: Once I went to the Galilee and saw a place that they were marking off, and they said: leprous stones were cleared out to there.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report backs up the first. A spot in the Galilee was marked as impure because stones with צרעת had been thrown there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says that stones with צרעת must be removed and dumped in an impure place outside the city. Finding such a place shows that house-צרעת actually happened, which adds force to the challenge against the 'never happened' ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage from the village of Akko
Marking off a place, as a warning that it is impure

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three 'never happened' ברייתות (בן סורר ומורה, עיר הנדחת, בית המנוגע) is matched to a particular תנא whose strict conditions make the case practically impossible: רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון, רבי אליעזר, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Each one is answered by eyewitness reports that it did happen.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ:
phrases.english: רבי שמעון of Kfar Akko said:
Once I went to the Galilee
and I saw a place that they were marking off,
and they said: leprous stones were cleared out to there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second eyewitness report that supports step 37's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That a בית המנוגע did actually happen
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון איש כפר עכו's sighting of a marked-off dump for leprous stones in the Galilee

steps.title: Parents with physical disabilities cannot bring a rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if either parent lacks hands, is lame, mute, blind or deaf, the son cannot become a בן סורר ומורה. It learns each exclusion from a different phrase in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the parents is without hands, lame, mute, blind or deaf, the son does not become a rebellious son. The פסוק says 'his father and mother shall grab him', so not parents without hands. 'They shall bring him out', so not lame parents. 'They shall say', so not mute parents. 'This son of ours', so not blind parents. 'He does not listen to our voice', so not deaf parents.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five physical conditions that disqualify a parent, and ties each one to a word in the פסוק about the rebellious son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a series of actions the parents perform: grabbing, bringing out, speaking, pointing ('this'), and hearing. The משנה reads each action as a requirement, so a parent who physically cannot do that action cannot bring the case. The son is not punished at all, even if the other parent is fully able.

keyTerms.meaning: A person without hands (or unable to use them)
A lame person, who cannot walk properly
A mute person, who cannot speak
The stubborn and rebellious son of דברים 21

steps.confusionAlert: 'One of them' means only ONE parent needs to have the condition. Even if the other parent is completely healthy, the son still cannot become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next question: is this exact, word-by-word reading of the פסוק a general rule for the whole Torah?

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If one of them was without hands,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the parents, the father and the mother.

phrases.english: or lame, or mute,
or blind, or deaf –
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son,
as it says: 'And his father and mother shall grab hold of him'
– and not those without hands,
'And they shall bring him out' – and not lame people,
'And they shall say' – and not mute people,
'This son of ours' – and not blind people,
'He does not listen to our voice' – and not deaf people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶם גִּידֵּם, אוֹ חִיגֵּר, אוֹ אִלֵּם, אוֹ סוֹמֵא, אוֹ חֵרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the side discussion about the leprous house; returns to the topic of בן סורר ומורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If either parent is without hands, lame, mute, blind or deaf, the son cannot become a בן סורר ומורה, learned from five phrases in the פסוק.

steps.title: The two-stage process: flogging first, then trial and stoning
steps.stepSummary: The son is first warned and flogged before three judges. If he sins again, he is tried by twenty-three, and he is stoned only if the original three judges are present, learned from 'this son of ours.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They warn him in front of three judges and flog him. If he goes back and acts badly again, he is judged by a court of twenty-three. He is not stoned unless the first three judges are there, because the פסוק says 'this son of ours', meaning this is the one who was flogged in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and explains the steps of the court process: first a warning and lashes, then, after another sin, a full capital trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rounds. Round one is a smaller court of three that warns and flogs him. Round two, only if he sins again, is a court of twenty-three for the death penalty. The word 'this' (זה) is read as pointing to the first three judges, so they must be there to recognize him as the same son they flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: They warn him (a formal warning before punishment)
He went back and sinned again
A court of twenty-three judges, needed for capital cases

steps.whatToRemember: The rebellious son is never stoned for his first offense. He is first warned and flogged before three; only a repeat offense brings a trial before twenty-three, and the original three must be present.
steps.whyThisMatters: Here too the word 'this' is read very literally, adding to the picture of how exactly the משנה reads this פסוק.

phrases.english: They warn him before three,
and they flog him.
If he went back and acted badly again –
he is judged by twenty-three,
and he is not stoned unless there are present
the first three,
phrases.notes: These are the same three judges who warned and flogged him in round one.

phrases.english: as it says: 'This son of ours' –
this is the one who was flogged before you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְרִין בּוֹ בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה, וּמַלְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from who qualifies as parents to the court procedure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First offense: warning and lashes before three. Repeat offense: trial before twenty-three, and stoning only with the first three judges present.

steps.title: Inference: must a verse be applied exactly as written?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that we can learn a general rule from the משנה: a פסוק must be fulfilled exactly according to its literal wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you learn from this that we need the פסוק to be fulfilled exactly as it is written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It proposes a broad lesson: since the משנה excluded disabled parents based on each literal word, maybe every פסוק in the Torah must be applied exactly as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treated each phrase ('grab', 'bring out', 'say', 'this', 'listen') as a strict requirement. The גמרא asks whether this proves a general principle, that the Torah's wording is always taken literally and not more loosely.

keyTerms.meaning: You can learn from it (an attempt to draw a rule from a source)
We require the verse to be fulfilled exactly as written

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet a conclusion. The גמרא is only suggesting a rule, and in the very next words it starts to push back.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
You can learn from it:
that we require a verse to be done just as it is written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle out of the משנה's literal reading of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The general principle that a פסוק must be fulfilled exactly according to its literal wording.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's exclusion of disabled parents based on each literal word of דברים 21:19-20.

steps.title: Pushback begins: this case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to reject the proof by saying the case of the rebellious son is special, so no general rule can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its rejection of the proof. It says 'here is different', and the reason why comes in the next words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection argues that the literal reading in this משנה may come from something unique to the rebellious son, not from a rule for the whole Torah. The specific reason is not given yet; it continues right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different (a way of saying this case is special)

phrases.english: Here it is different,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attempted proof from step 41 by marking the rebellious son case as an exception.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning a general Torah-wide rule from this משנה, without arguing with the משנה's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the literal reading applies everywhere, but the rebellious son case may have its own special reason for it (explained next).
